_schema: The NL-phrasing sub-dictionary (Rival-authored, 2026-08-06). Per action id: readings [{sentence, stance, binds, via, resolution}]. stance ∈ imperative | outcome | future-anchored | corrective | deictic | composite | gated. binds maps each of the action's args to how the sentence references it. via lists other action ids the resolution routes through (empty when direct). resolution is the one-line recovery: how the sentence maps back to the canonical press+args.
_note: Companion to ACTIONS.json (the working mirror alongside this file) — the fourth leg of the word interface: press (dictionary), read (blackboard), write (corp-command), and now PHRASING (how far a sentence can stand from the command and still resolve to it).

Purpose (Ben, 2026-08-06): a rich dictionary of SENTENCES, not aliases. Each sentence is a path back to the intended output, and may consider future use of the action (future-anchored stance). Every reading doubles as a labelled training pair for the compressed local model (BL-279 corpus leg) — the dictionary does the reasoning work so the small model doesn't have to.

Stance taxonomy settled 2026-08-06: imperative (direct restatement), outcome (names the result, resolved via expected_output), future-anchored (justified by a later action's preconditions), corrective (names a problem; resolves to a candidate set disambiguated by blackboard state), deictic (action plain, args contextual), composite (one sentence, a legal sequence), gated (asks for something currently illegal; resolves to the enabling action). future-anchored and gated are the same relation seen from opposite ends — both carry `via`.

Register drift (ancient/divine idiom) is deliberately NOT in this file — era-voiced variants live in the 0 CE test battery (SANDBOX-0CE.md), which tests whether these resolutions survive a register shift.
Pilot scope: the gameplay family only (11 entries). Canvas/lens/ledger/chrome phrasings wait until the pilot proves the shape.

AMENDMENT (Battery A run 1, 2026-08-06 — annals/battery-0ce-A-run1.md): stance is a SET, not a scalar. A sentence can be corrective AND composite (A5), corrective AND outcome (A7). Readings below keep a single primary stance; resolvers must not be penalised for choosing a defensible secondary one. Action resolution scored 10/10 under full register drift, so the taxonomy's action axis is validated as-is.
Landing path: this file is Rival's design artifact; it lands into Io (as a `readings` field in ACTIONS.json or a sibling file, Io's call) via an explicit backlog item, never by silent merge.

readings.sentence: Raise an iron extraction site on the tile we just selected.
readings.resolution: Direct restatement: press the iron extraction row in the construction ledger on the selected tile.

readings.sentence: Get iron flowing into our pool from this deposit.

binds.type: inferred: extraction_site is the only type whose output is pool stock of a raw resource

readings.resolution: Match desired state ('iron in the pool') to the action whose expected_output produces it: build extraction_site targeting iron on the deposit tile.

readings.sentence: We will need propellant on hand before the launchpad can earn its keep — lay in the refinery now.

binds.tile: a tile with the refinery recipe available, agent's choice

readings.resolution: The named future press (launchpad operation) has an input need this build satisfies; resolve to build processing_facility with the propellant recipe, sited ahead of demand.

readings.sentence: Another one, same as this, right here.
readings.resolution: The alternate press exists for exactly this sentence: 'Build another here' on the selected owned building, gated by stack capacity.

readings.sentence: Open a route to sea for this region's goods.

binds.tile: a coastal tile in the region

readings.resolution: The output 'cheaper off-body/coastal freight' belongs to the port; resolve to build port on a coastal tile — the precondition (coast) narrows the tile bind.

readings.sentence: Put a launchpad on this world.

binds.tile: any legal tile on the body

readings.resolution: If the body is unsurveyed the build is illegal — the sentence resolves first to survey (the enabling press), then to build launchpad; note the per-body cap of 1.

readings.sentence: Tear the old wharf down — we need the ground.
readings.resolution: Direct: select the building, Demolish, confirm. The stated reason ('need the ground') matches the doc's only good reason — the tile is worth more re-purposed.

readings.sentence: Clear this tile for the smelter we are about to raise.

binds.building: whatever currently occupies the capacity-capped tile

readings.resolution: The future build's precondition (a free slot) is what demolition provides; demolish the occupant, then build. Irreversible and refundless — only correct when the successor is decided.

readings.sentence: This mine is finished; the seam is empty and it will never pay again.
readings.resolution: A loss-maker normally resolves to idle (reversible), but 'never pay again' removes the option value — a depleted deposit resolves past idle to demolish. Blackboard check: deposit remaining ≈ 0.

readings.sentence: Shut the smelter down for now, but keep it.
readings.resolution: 'For now, but keep it' is exactly idle's contract — reversible, asset retained, tile held.

readings.sentence: Stop the bleeding at the steelworks.
readings.resolution: Names a problem, not a press. Candidate set: set_recipe (if another recipe clears better), set_workforce (throttle), idle (stop wages entirely). Disambiguate on blackboard: no profitable recipe and no acceptable throttle → idle.

readings.sentence: Mothball everything on that continent until prices recover.

binds.building: each running owned building on the named continent, one press per building

readings.resolution: Decomposes to one idle press per building; 'until prices recover' pre-registers the future resume trigger, it is not an argument.

readings.sentence: Wake the smelter back up.
readings.resolution: Direct: select the idled building, Resume.

readings.sentence: Steel is clearing high again — capture it with what we already own.

binds.building: idled buildings whose output is steel

readings.resolution: 'With what we already own' excludes build (capex); the zero-capex margin-capture press on an idled asset is resume. This is the doc's own signal: prices recovered.

readings.sentence: Lay a track through the pass between the mine and the market town.

binds.tile: each tile on the named route, one press per tile

readings.resolution: One place_road press per tile along the route; 'track' names tier 1.

readings.sentence: Our ore is paying too much to reach the smelter.

binds.tile: the tiles the ore freight actually traverses (blackboard: route)
binds.road_tier: lowest tier whose saving beats its cost

readings.resolution: High haul cost on a real freight lane resolves to roads along that lane — the doc's own criterion: worth it on tiles carrying real freight.

readings.sentence: Upgrade the road to a highway before the new port opens and traffic doubles.

binds.tile: tiles on the port's inland approach

readings.resolution: The future press (port build) creates the freight this tier-raise serves; upgrade-in-place is legal since current level is below 3.

readings.sentence: List two hundred grain a quarter on the home market, but take nothing under 4.
readings.resolution: Direct: Sell Orders tab on the home body's market, resource + quantity + floor as stated.

readings.sentence: Don't let our copper be dumped into this crash.

binds.floor_price: above the crashed price, at the acceptable minimum

readings.resolution: Floor-protection is this action's stated purpose; place a sell order whose floor sits above the crash. WARNING the resolution must carry: the triple leaves the auto-sell path — a floor set too high stockpiles silently.

readings.sentence: Hold half the steel back — the shipyard will want it next year.
readings.resolution: Rationing toward a future construction spend: a metered order (reduced quantity, floor 0) replaces auto-sell-everything, keeping stock for the named future build's material bill.

readings.sentence: Cancel the copper order on the home market.
readings.resolution: Direct: Remove on the matching row.

readings.sentence: The copper is piling up and selling nothing — let the market have it again.

binds.order: the standing copper order whose floor cleared nothing

readings.resolution: The silent-stockpile failure mode of a too-high floor; removing the last order returns the triple to auto-sell. If control should be kept at a lower floor, the path is remove then re-add (there is no edit).

readings.sentence: Switch the plant to rations.
readings.resolution: Direct: production-method combo, pick the rations row.

readings.sentence: Steel is losing money here; make this plant earn.

binds.recipe: the recipe with the best local margin (blackboard: per-recipe clearing prices)

readings.resolution: First lever on a processor, free of capex — try the recipe switch before idle. Disambiguation: if no recipe clears profitably, fall through to idle.

readings.sentence: Every new plant we raise starts on steel — put this one to its real work.

binds.recipe: the recipe the build was priced on / intended for

readings.resolution: The doc's own note: new processors default to steel, so set_recipe is typically the first press after building one. 'Its real work' binds to the intent recorded at build time.

readings.sentence: Run the mine at half crew.
readings.resolution: Direct: untick Auto, set the slider to 50. Note the side effect the resolution must carry: a manual value pins the dial (clears workforce_auto).

readings.sentence: Feed the smelter whatever ore it takes, even if the mine itself runs at a loss.

binds.workforce: above 100, sized to the smelter's input demand

readings.resolution: Overdrive past 100% to feed a downstream chain at a per-building loss — the doc's own third case. The downstream building's input need sizes the value.

readings.sentence: Park the quarry cheaply but keep the crew ready to return.
readings.resolution: Staff-to-0 versus idle is a real fork: workforce 0 stops wages but keeps the building formally running. Resolve to set_workforce 0 when the sentence implies fast per-tick recovery; idle when it implies a season-scale stop.

readings.sentence: Hand the staffing back to the solver.
readings.resolution: Direct: tick Auto. Mostly exists to undo an earlier manual pin — fresh builds start with it on.

readings.sentence: Stop micromanaging that mill; just let it make what it can.
readings.resolution: 'Let it maximise its own profit' is exactly the solver's contract; resolve to set_workforce_auto.

readings.sentence: Dispatch a survey to the second moon.
readings.resolution: Direct: select the body, Dispatch Survey. Cost debited up front; results arrive region-by-region.

readings.sentence: We are running out of ground here — find the next place worth digging.

binds.body: an unsurveyed body chosen by cost/ETA against the balance

readings.resolution: Tile saturation at home is the doc's own trigger for discovery spend; resolve to survey the cheapest promising hidden body within the solvency floor.

readings.sentence: Before we commit to a launchpad there, we must know what the ground holds.
readings.resolution: The future build's evaluation needs surveyed tiles; survey is the enabling press. Same relation as the gated reading of build, seen from the forward end.
